transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. Can you tell me what brings you in today?

Hi, doctor. Thank you so much for taking the time to see me. 

Um... well, I came in because the doctor who was doing my insurance physical recently told me that my weight was too low. I hope I'm not wasting your time with this, but he seemed like he wanted me to get it checked out, so I wanted to make sure I followed up. 

Honestly, to me, I just look lean, you know? I'm a painting worker, so I'm constantly up and down ladders and working really long days... it just keeps me pretty active and burns a lot of energy. But I wanted to do what he asked and make sure everything is okay. Does that make sense?
Have you noticed any unintentional weight loss recently, or have you been losing weight without trying?

Well, um... I wouldn't really say it's unintentional, exactly. I mean, I haven't been trying to drop pounds or anything, but... I guess I just don't eat a whole lot during the day. I hope that doesn't sound bad. 

It's just that most days I keep it to coffee in the morning, and maybe I'll grab a protein bar between paint jobs if I have a second. And then I'll just have a small dinner at night. Honestly, eating a full meal during the day just feels like it would really slow me down when I need to be climbing up and down the ladders, you know? I just want to stay light on my feet so I can do a good job for my clients. 

Is... is that the kind of thing you're looking for? I'm just trying to figure out what the other doctor was so worried about.
Have you ever felt that your weight or the way you look is excessively important to how you feel about yourself, or have you been avoiding eating because you're worried about gaining weight?

Um... well, I wouldn't say I'm completely obsessed with it or anything like that. I mean, I don't want you to think I'm standing in front of a mirror all day. But... I guess I do care about it a little bit? I hope that's normal. 

Like, sometimes when I finish a job, I'll take a picture next to the mural or the house I just painted, just to show the clients or put on my website. And... well, if I catch a glimpse of myself in the mirror or in those photos, and my stomach or my face doesn't look, um, sharp enough? Like, if I don't look lean and fit... it kind of ruins the whole day for me. I just feel like I need to look a certain way to represent my business well, you know? 

I don't really avoid eating just to lose weight, exactly, it's more just... I want to make sure I keep that sharp look. Does that make sense? I hope I'm explaining this right.
When you look at yourself and feel disappointed if you don’t look lean enough, is that mainly because you’re worried about gaining weight, or is it more about how you see yourself overall?

Um... well, I guess it's a little bit of both? I really hope I don't sound too, um, vain or anything by saying this. But... yeah, I suppose I am a little worried about gaining weight. 

Like, if I have to go to a client dinner, or if I end up eating something a bit heavier, like bread... if I step on the scale the next morning and it's gone up even just a tiny little bit, I do get kind of tense about it. It's nothing crazy, I promise! I just... I'll usually start cutting back the next day, just to make sure the weight doesn't stick. 

I figure it's just a good way to keep things balanced and stay in shape for work, right? Is it normal to feel a little stressed about that kind of thing? I just want to make sure I'm giving you the right answers here.

Have you ever found yourself so focused on controlling your weight or shape that it started to interfere with your daily life, like affecting your work, relationships, or causing you to avoid social situations?

Oh, no, it definitely hasn't interfered with my work! I want to make sure you know that. I've still been getting all my painting jobs done right on schedule, and I always make sure my clients are really happy with the results. 

But, um... I guess with the social stuff... maybe a little bit? I really hope that doesn't make me sound rude or antisocial. It's just... I do tend to avoid some of those client meals, or even just regular social plans with friends lately. 

It's not because I don't care about them! It's just that if we go out to eat, I know the situation is probably going to turn into people commenting on what I'm eating, or asking why I'm not having more, or they'll say something about how I look. And I just really don't want to make things awkward or have everyone focusing on me like that. So it's just easier to politely bow out of those situations, you know? 

I mean, I think a lot of people probably prefer to avoid awkward dinners anyway, right? I hope that's an okay answer. I'm really not trying to let it affect my life too much.

After eating something you consider heavy or indulgent, do you ever find yourself exercising more than usual, skipping meals, or doing anything else specifically to try to burn off or compensate for those calories?

Um... oh, no, definitely not. I mean, I know I said earlier that I might cut back a little bit the next day, but I don't do anything extreme like skipping meals entirely or going out and running for hours. I really want to make sure you know I'm not punishing myself or doing anything crazy like that. 

My painting work is pretty physical anyway, you know, being up and down ladders and moving heavy equipment around all day. So I don't really feel the need to do extra workouts just to burn off a meal. I wouldn't want to overdo it and end up too tired to do a good job for my clients. 

If I have a heavier meal, I just try to eat a little lighter the next day, like maybe having a salad instead of a sandwich. Just what a normal person would do if they had a big dinner, right? I really try to be sensible about it. I hope that sounds reasonable to you? I just want to make sure I'm handling things the right way.

Outside of avoiding certain social events, have you noticed any other ways your concerns about weight or shape might have affected other areas of your life, like your mood, personal relationships, or ability to focus on work?

Um... well, no, not really. I mean, I definitely wouldn't say it's affected my mood or my relationships or anything like that. I really try to be easygoing and not let things get to me. 

My focus at work is totally fine, I promise! Like I said, I always make sure my clients get exactly what they asked for. I wouldn't let anything get in the way of doing a good job. 

I guess... I mean, maybe sometimes I get a little quiet if I'm thinking about what I'm going to eat later, or if I'm feeling a little stressed about, you know, staying on track. But it's nothing that really bothers anyone else, I don't think. I always try to keep a smile on my face and just keep working hard. 

Most people probably have moments where they get a little distracted by their own thoughts, right? It's just normal stuff. I really hope I'm not making it sound like a bigger deal than it is. Does that make sense?
Have you ever found yourself eating a much larger amount of food in a short period than you normally would, and felt like you couldn’t stop or control how much you were eating?

Oh, no. Um... no, I've never done anything like that. I always make sure I'm really careful about what I eat, so I've never had a time where I felt out of control or ate a huge amount all at once. 

I really wouldn't want you to think I just sit around stuffing myself—I try really hard to be good and stay disciplined with my portions. I mean, I think it's pretty normal to want to stay in control of what you're eating, right? I just like to keep things neat and manageable, the same way I try to be with my painting jobs. I hope that's a good thing? I just really wouldn't want to lose control like that.
Have you ever made yourself vomit or used laxatives, diuretics, or diet pills to control your weight?

Oh, gosh, no. Um... absolutely not. I would never do anything like that. That sounds... well, really dangerous, you know? 

I just stick to being careful with my portions and eating clean. I don't take any kind of pills or... or make myself sick or anything like that. I really want to take care of my body, especially since I need my strength to do a good job painting and hauling my gear around. 

I'd really hate for you to think I was doing something extreme or harmful to myself. I just try to have good willpower and keep things on track, which is a positive thing, right? I'm just trying to be healthy and safe about it, I promise.
Do you feel that your weight or body shape plays a major role in how you judge yourself or your overall sense of identity?

Um... well, I wouldn't say it's my whole identity or anything like that. I really pride myself on my work and being a reliable guy, first and foremost. 

But... I guess I do care about it a fair amount. I think most people want to look their best, right? Like... sometimes when I catch myself in a mirror, or if someone takes a photo of me standing next to one of my finished murals... I kind of end up judging the whole day by whether my stomach and my face look sharp enough. 

I just really want to look fit and put-together, especially when I'm representing my business. I promise it's not like a huge vanity thing or anything, and I don't let it stop me from getting my work done. I just like to make sure I'm maintaining my standards and keeping my edge. That's a pretty normal way to feel, isn't it? I hope I'm not making it sound worse than it is.
Do you find that concerns about your weight or appearance ever interfere with your ability to enjoy life or feel at ease in your day-to-day activities?

Um... I wouldn't say it interferes with my life, really. I mean, I'm still getting all my painting jobs done, and I'm always on time for my clients. I make sure my work never suffers, I promise you that. 

But... I guess, maybe sometimes I do skip out on things. Like, if a client wants to buy me lunch after a job, or... or if some of the guys are going out to grab food, I usually just say I'm busy. I just... I really don't want to be in a situation where people are watching what I eat, or, you know, making comments about my food or how I look. It just feels easier to avoid it so I don't make anyone uncomfortable or draw attention to myself. 

I'm still functioning perfectly fine, though! I just prefer to keep my meals private so I can stay focused. That's okay to do, right? I just want to make sure I'm not doing anything wrong by wanting a little privacy.
Would you say that your weight or body shape is something you consider to be very important in how you judge yourself, more so than most people might?

Um... I don't think it's more important to me than it is for most guys. I mean, everybody wants to look decent, right? 

I really don't think I'm obsessed with it or anything. I just... I like to be presentable. I don't think I judge myself harder than anyone else does. I mean, maybe I'm a little hard on myself sometimes, but that's just because I want to be the best version of me, you know? It's not like I'm constantly obsessing over every little detail. 

I really hope you don't think I'm completely wrapped up in my appearance. I'm just a normal guy trying to stay in shape. That's pretty standard, isn't it?
Have you ever felt distressed or upset about your body shape or weight, even when other people might not see a problem?

Um... well, no, not really. I mean, sure, sometimes I might look in the mirror and think I could tighten up a bit, but I don't get really upset or distressed about it. 

I think most guys have days where they feel a little off, right? Like, maybe their clothes fit a little differently or something. But it's nothing major. I definitely don't lose sleep over it or let it ruin my day. I just kind of brush it off and keep working. 

People usually tell me I look fine, and I trust them. I wouldn't want to make a big deal out of nothing. I'm just trying to stay healthy, you know? That's what you're supposed to do, right? I'm not overreacting to anything, I promise.
Have you experienced any physical symptoms like dizziness, fatigue, or difficulty concentrating that might be related to your eating habits?

Um... no, not really. I mean, my job is pretty physical, so being a little tired at the end of the day is just... well, it's just part of the job, you know? Painting all day, going up and down ladders, it takes it out of you. 

I definitely don't get dizzy or anything like that. And my concentration is great! I have to be really focused to get the edges right and make sure the clients are happy. I'm always on top of my work. 

If I'm ever a little fatigued, it's just from working hard, not from what I eat. I make sure I have enough energy to do a good job. That makes sense, right? Anyone would be a little tired after a long day of physical labor, don't you think? I'm doing okay, I promise.
Do you feel that your body shape or weight influences how you see yourself, even if others tell you that you look fine or seem healthy?

Um... well, maybe just a little? I mean, I really try not to let it get to me. But... I guess sometimes, like if I catch myself in a mirror, or if there's a photo of me standing next to one of my murals after I finish a big job... I do kind of focus on it. 

If I look at the picture and my stomach or my face doesn't look, you know, sharp enough... I guess I sort of judge the whole day by that. It can kind of put a damper on things if I feel like I look soft. 

But I think that's mostly just because I take pride in my work and I want to look good standing next to it, you know? It's totally normal to want to look fit in photos, right? I hope that doesn't sound too vain or anything. I just want to look professional and put-together. That's pretty common, don't you think?
Would you say that your concerns about your weight or shape influence how you feel about yourself most days, even if just to some degree?

Um... yeah, I guess so. Just to some degree, like you said. I mean, it's not like it ruins my whole life or anything, I promise. But... yeah, if I'm being honest, it does kind of sit in the back of my mind. 

Like I was saying before, if I catch a glimpse of myself in the mirror, or if I see a photo of me next to a finished mural... if my stomach isn't completely flat, or if my face looks a little full... it just kind of bothers me. I'll sort of judge the whole day based on whether I looked sharp enough in that moment. 

It just makes me feel like I need to work harder, you know? Like I'm slacking off. But I don't let it get out of hand. It's just a little bit of self-improvement, which is a good thing, right? I'm just trying to hold myself to a good standard. That's okay to do, isn't it?
Would you say that your concerns about your weight or shape influence how you feel about yourself to the point where it causes you significant distress or affects your daily life in any way?

Um... well, it definitely doesn't stop me from working, I can promise you that. I'm still getting all my painting jobs done right on schedule, and my clients are really happy with the work. I would never let anything get in the way of my job. 

But... I guess, maybe socially, it affects things just a little bit? Like... sometimes a client will offer to buy me lunch, or some of the guys want to grab food after a big job, and... I usually just say I'm too busy or I have somewhere to be. 

It's just... I really don't want to be in a situation where people are watching what I'm eating, or making comments about my food, or... or saying things about how I look. It just makes me feel really uncomfortable, you know? So it's just easier to avoid those meals altogether. 

That doesn't mean it's causing me "significant distress," though, right? I mean, lots of people prefer to eat alone or just don't like big social meals. It's just a preference, really. That's pretty normal, don't you think?
Would you say that your sense of self-worth depends strongly on your weight or body shape, more than it does for most people?

Well... I know I keep bringing this up, but... yeah, maybe it does a little bit. Like I was saying before about the mirrors, or those photos I take next to my murals when a job is done. If I look at them and my stomach or my face doesn't look sharp enough... I really do judge the whole day by that. Like, my whole mood and how I feel about myself as a person just kind of hinges on it in that moment. 

But I don't know if it's *that* much more than most people, right? I mean, everyone wants to feel confident and put-together. I just happen to be a little hard on myself if I don't look the part. I really hope you don't think I'm just being incredibly vain or shallow. I just tie a lot of my pride to my work and how I present myself alongside it. It's pretty normal to want to look your best and feel good about it, isn't it?
